headline: The 2017 tax law, enacted December 22, 2017, cut individual and corporate income tax rates and changed many deductions, credits, and business rules, and it opened part of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge to oil and gas leasing.
what_it_does: The law lowered the corporate tax rate to a flat 21 percent and changed individual income tax brackets, the standard deduction, and the child tax credit, most of them on a temporary basis through 2025. It also limited or removed many itemized deductions, such as state and local tax deductions above $10,000 and the deduction for moving expenses, and it repealed the individual mandate penalty for not having health insurance. The law created a new 20 percent deduction for many pass-through business owners and expanded expensing rules for business equipment and property. It also set up a federal oil and gas leasing program for the Coastal Plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge in Alaska.

who_it_affects.how: Many itemized deductions were limited or suspended, including state and local taxes above $10,000, home equity loan interest, and miscellaneous deductions subject to the 2% floor.

who_it_affects.group: Married couples and heads of household with children
who_it_affects.how: The law raised the standard deduction and the child tax credit, which lowers taxable income or tax owed for many families with children under 17.

who_it_affects.group: Owners of pass-through businesses such as partnerships, S corporations, and sole proprietorships
who_it_affects.how: They may deduct 20 percent of qualified business income, subject to wage and income limits, with restrictions for certain service businesses like health, law, and consulting.
The corporate income tax rate dropped to a flat 21 percent, and the corporate alternative minimum tax was repealed.

who_it_affects.group: People who buy health insurance on their own
who_it_affects.how: The penalty for not maintaining minimum essential health coverage was reduced to zero beginning in 2019.

who_it_affects.group: Owners of estates and gifts above the old exemption level
who_it_affects.how: The estate and gift tax exemption doubled to $10 million, indexed for inflation, for estates of people who die or gifts made in 2018 through 2025.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses that buy equipment or property
who_it_affects.how: They may expense 100 percent of the cost of qualifying property placed in service after September 27, 2017, and before 2023, with the amount phasing down after that.

who_it_affects.group: Students with federal or private student loans discharged due to death or total and permanent disability
who_it_affects.how: Those discharged loans are excluded from taxable income for a temporary period.
The deduction for living expenses incurred by Members of Congress was eliminated.

who_it_affects.group: Residents and businesses in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge Coastal Plain area and oil and gas companies
who_it_affects.how: The Interior Department must hold at least two lease sales within 10 years, each with at least 400,000 acres, and may authorize up to 2,000 surface acres for production facilities.

when_it_takes_effect: Most individual provisions apply to tax years beginning after December 31, 2017, and many expire after December 31, 2025, while corporate rate changes apply starting in 2018.
